newsitem.title: UK: British factory gate prices fall in June.
newsitem.headline: British factory gate prices fall in June.

text.p: Prices of goods leaving Britain's factory gates fell by 0.2 percent in June, the Office for National Statistics said on Monday, reversing the 0.2 percent rise seen in May.
In the year to June, prices rose 1.1, modestly higher than the yearly rate in May of 1.0 percent.
The costs of raw material for British firms fell too, down 0.8 percent in June on a seasonally adjusted basis.
In the last year manufacturers have seen costs fall by 8.6 percent, thanks to the strength of the pound and sharp falls in the prices of oil and other commodities.
City analysts said cheaper input prices will help firms cope with slower sales of their goods abroad, another result of the strong pound.

"Lower input prices will help mitigate the trouble the exchange rate is causing for manufacturers. Their margins are probably still growing because of these low costs," said David Philpotts, UK economist at Schroders.
